items.name: Strive
items.headline: Bitcoin funding plans meet the execution test
items.fact: The Block reported that Strive's CEO discussed potential funding from warrants expiring in October. The larger Bitcoin accumulation scenario was conditional, not his base case.
items.bullCase: Some investors have the right to buy new Strive shares. If they buy, Strive gets more cash. More cash could buy more Bitcoin. That could help, but it does not mean the stock must go up.
items.watchFor: Check company filings for actual warrant exercises and Bitcoin per share. Separate completed purchases from management targets.
items.risk: New shares can dilute existing holders. Bitcoin can fall, and potential warrant proceeds are not guaranteed.

items.name: Robinhood Markets
items.headline: Robinhood expands prediction markets with OG.com
items.fact: Robinhood and OG.com announced a multi-year prediction-markets partnership. The announcement says Robinhood will hold equity stakes in Crypto.com and OG.com, with a phased rollout to eligible U.S. customers beginning September 8.
items.bullCase: More contracts could bring more trading. More trading could bring more fee revenue. That depends on customers using the product; a deal alone does not guarantee growth.
items.watchFor: Check actual customer use, trading volume, and revenue in future company reports. Compare the results with the cost of expanding.
items.risk: Competition, regulatory limits, and weak demand could reduce the benefit. Event contracts carry substantial loss risk; this is company research, not a suggestion to trade them.
